mutants.description: Loss-aversion identification counts a mixed lottery only on the B side of each question, so a set whose only mixed lottery is A is refused.
The logit likelihood takes its certainty equivalents from the CRRA model at the current gamma (wealth fixed at 1000 dollars) instead of the prospect value.
The estimator discards every response whose two lotteries are both pure before maximising, so the likelihood uses only the mixed questions.
Observed information with the sign of every mixed second derivative flipped, so the cross-parameter covariances are wrong.
Reported log_likelihood is the value at the start point of the search, not at the estimate.
Prospect certainty equivalent of a negative lottery value returns a positive amount: the minus sign of the loss-branch inverse is dropped.
Student error: loss aversion counts a response only when both of its lotteries mix a gain and a loss, so a set whose mixed lottery sits on one side alone is refused.
Student error: the reported loss aversion is clamped at 10 (a bound the page never states), so a participant whose estimate is above 10 is reported at 10.
log_likelihood trusts its input: the probability checks (non-negative, sum exactly 1) are skipped.
The standard errors use the observed information by central differences of step 1e-3, not 1e-5 or 1e-6.
The prospect model refuses a final wealth (wealth plus prize) of zero or below, although it does not use wealth.
Probabilities are summed as floats and compared with 1.0, so a sum off by less than float resolution is accepted.
Standard errors use the observed information at a fixed start point (0, 0, 0) instead of at the estimate.
At gamma = 0 the CRRA certainty equivalent is rounded with Python's round(), which sends an exact half to even.
log_likelihood returns the mean log-likelihood per response instead of the sum.
A gain of zero probability counts as a gain when the lottery is tested for mixing a gain and a loss.
Standard errors from the outer product of the per-response scores (BHHH), not from the observed information.
Probabilities are checked to sum to 1 after the float sum is rounded to twelve places.
Probability text is read through float() before Fraction, so "1/3" is refused as not a number.
The prospect model ignores the lambda parameter and uses loss aversion 1 in every certainty equivalent.
The observed information drops its off-diagonal terms, so the covariances between the parameters are ignored.
The standard error of lambda multiplies by lambda twice, as if the coordinate change were exp(2 a).
CRRA certainty equivalent divides the expected utility by (1 - gamma) before the inverse power, applying the factor twice.
log_likelihood reads the choice precision from the lambda key of params, a key-name slip, so kappa is set to lambda.
estimate reads each response without checking that its probabilities are non-negative and sum to exactly 1 (log_likelihood still checks).
Observed information cross terms use forward differences (one-sided, step 1e-5) instead of central differences; the diagonal stays central.
The reported log_likelihood is the negative of the likelihood at the estimate, a sign slip in the return.
Each probability is rounded to the nearest fraction with denominator at most 1000 before the exact sum check, so a sum that is off by 1e-13 is accepted.
The CRRA wealth check compares the absolute value of wealth plus prize with zero, so a negative final wealth passes the check and is sent to the power function.
The search clamps log kappa at zero inside the objective, so a choice precision below 1 is fitted as if it were 1 and the estimate is not the maximum.
The reported kappa_hat is clamped to at least 1, so a choice precision below 1 is reported as 1 while the
A zero prize with positive probability counts as a gain in the mixed-sign test, so a set whose only 'gain' is a sure zero passes the mixed-sign condition.
The gamma standard error omits the factor gamma (1 - gamma) that carries zeta to gamma, so it is the standard error in the logit coordinate.
The logit reads the certainty-equivalent difference in dollars, not in units of $100, so every kappa is off by a factor of 100.
The Newton search stops once the largest gradient component is below 1e-3, so the estimate is returned before it is a stationary point.
A zero prize with positive probability counts as a loss in the mixed-sign test, so a set whose only gain is paired with a sure zero prize passes the mixed-sign condition.
The mixed-sign condition looks only at the lottery each participant chose, so a mixed lottery that was not chosen does not count.
The prospect certainty equivalent of a negative lottery value divides by lambda after the power, not before it, so the loss branch is wrong whenever lambda is not 1.
CRRA at gamma = 0 sums the expected prize in float, so an exact half cent can round down.
Loss value puts lambda inside the power, -(lambda (-x))^(1-gamma), not outside it.
The prospect model refuses wealth plus prize <= 0, although the prospect model does not use wealth.
estimate returns the best starting-grid point and never runs the search, so it is a grid point.
Choice log-probability written as log of the logistic 1/(1+exp(-z)), which overflows for large negative z.
The estimate fields are rounded to four decimals before they are returned, to match the printed output.
The likelihood sum starts at the second response, so the first choice is left out of every likelihood.
Standard errors take 1/sqrt of each diagonal entry of the information, ignoring the off-diagonal terms.
CRRA refuses final wealth below zero but accepts exactly zero, so a prize that takes wealth to zero is not refused.
The loss weight lambda multiplies the gain branch of the value function as well as the loss branch.
The prospect model values the lottery on final wealth (wealth plus each prize) instead of on the change from 0.
An unknown model name raises TypeError, where the specification names ValueError.
Unknown model name raises KeyError from a dict lookup, where the page requires ValueError naming the two allowed models.
At gamma = 0 the exact expected prize is rounded with an exact half going down (ceil of x minus one half), against the page's toward-plus-infinity rule.
Probabilities that sum above 1 are accepted; only a sum below 1 is refused.
A negative probability is accepted whenever the probabilities sum to exactly 1.
The CRRA wealth check looks only at the first prize, so a later prize can take final wealth below zero.
The prospect inverse divides a positive lottery value by lambda, as if it were a loss.
The logit uses z = -kappa (CE_A - CE_B), so the more valuable alternative is less likely to be chosen.
The standard error of lambda omits the delta-method factor lambda (it is the standard error in log lambda).
The standard error of kappa is kappa times the variance, not the square root of it.
The model name is folded to lower case for the check but the original spelling is passed on, so CRRA takes the prospect branch.
At gamma = 0 the expected prize is floored, so an exact half cent goes down.
Prospect certainty equivalent on the loss side omits the loss weight lambda in the inverse.
Mixed-sign check passes when some response has a gain and some response has a loss, not in one lottery.
Log-likelihood scores every response as if the participant chose A, ignoring the recorded choice.
The wealth-plus-prize error message omits the text the exception table quotes.
Gain test uses x >= 0, so a zero prize with positive probability counts as a gain for mixed-sign identification.
CRRA certainty equivalent takes the inverse power 1/gamma instead of 1/(1-gamma).
CRRA certainty equivalent with no log limit: gamma = 1 divides by zero instead of using ln W.
CRRA certainty equivalent set to the expected prize, ignoring risk aversion.
CRRA certainty equivalent computed as u inverse of u of the expected wealth, not of expected utility.
Loss aversion multiplies the gains instead of the losses (the kink of the value function is reversed).
Prospect certainty equivalent pairs the sorted prizes with the probabilities in their listed order.
Log-likelihood omits the log(1 - P) term for the alternative that was not chosen.
Estimate skips the mixed-sign check, so pure-gain responses are fitted instead of refused.
CRRA accepts final wealth at or below zero and passes it to a power function.
Probabilities accepted when their sum is within one part in a hundred of 1, not exactly 1.
The CRRA certainty equivalent is rounded to two decimals before the half-cent rule, which is a second rounding.
The standard error of gamma omits the delta-method factor gamma(1 - gamma) from the logit coordinate.
Standard errors are taken from the reciprocal of the diagonal of the observed information, ignoring covariances.
Student error: the likelihood uses certainty equivalents rounded to whole cents, not the unrounded values the conventions require.
Student error: the reported loss aversion is clamped at 10 (a bound the page never states).
Student error: the maximiser runs three Newton iterations and reports the last iterate without a convergence check.
Student error: a prize with probability exactly zero is refused, although the page allows a probability of zero.

Standard errors use the observed information by central differences of step 1e-4 instead of the step of the reference, which moves the lambda standard error by more than 10 percent on some participants.
The Newton search stops once every partial derivative is below 1e-4, so the estimate is returned before it is a stationary point to the tolerance the page states.
The mixed-sign test ignores probabilities, so a lottery whose gain or loss has probability zero counts as mixed.
Probabilities are normalised instead of refused when they do not sum to 1.
The prospect inverse for a non-negative lottery value uses the exponent 1 - gamma instead of 1/(1 - gamma).
Logit log term computed as log(1 + exp(t)) without the stable form, so it overflows for large |z|.
The standard error of kappa is reported in log kappa: the factor kappa of the coordinate change is left out.
Student error: the prospect certainty equivalent takes the root of a negative lottery value directly, so every loss-only lottery raises ValueError.
Student error: the CRRA certainty equivalent is returned as final wealth, not as the change from wealth the conventions require.
Student error: loss aversion is accepted only when a lottery of A mixes a gain and a loss, so a set whose only mixed lottery is on the B side is refused.
Student error: the maximiser stops once one Newton step raises the log-likelihood by less than 1e-9, a function-value rule that stops before the gradient is near zero.
Student error: the CRRA model takes final wealth as wealth minus each prize, so a gain lowers final wealth.
Student error: estimate returns the printed Lab 3 numbers for any questionnaire of twelve responses, without maximising.
Student error: when the Newton search raises, the maximiser returns the best grid start as if it were the estimate.
Student error: the standard error of gamma carries the factor gamma instead of gamma (1 - gamma) from the change of coordinates.
Student error: a search whose step has become negligible is returned as the estimate without checking that the score is near zero.
Student error: the maximiser takes at most five damped Newton steps and returns the point it has reached, whether or not the score is near zero.
Student error: the maximiser stops as soon as every score component is below 1e-4, so an estimate can keep a score component of several times 1e-5.
Student error: a response that chose B contributes log P(A), not log(1 - P(A)), to the log-likelihood.
Student error: the estimate reports 1 - gamma_hat as gamma_hat (the probability of B instead of A in the curvature parameter).
Prospect value multiplies gains by lambda as well as losses, so the gain branch depends on lambda.
Logit uses the certainty-equivalent difference in units of one dollar (divides by 100), not the stated $100 unit.
Estimate reads only the first twelve responses (the size of the worked example) and ignores the rest.
CRRA log case (gamma = 1) takes the logs of the prizes instead of the logs of final wealth.
Estimate is memoised by the number of responses, so a second participant with the same count gets the first answer.
Standard errors are multiplied by the square root of the number of responses, as if they were a mean's.
Estimate returns the best grid point without running the Newton search, so the score is not zero at the estimate.
Certainty equivalent rounded by truncation toward zero instead of half up, so 2.5 cents gives 2.
Standard errors read from the observed information itself, not from its inverse (no inversion before the root).
Mixed-sign identification test counts a loss of probability zero as a loss, so a pure-gain design passes.
Newton search capped at five iterations, so a start far from the maximum stops before the score is zero.
Probabilities accepted when their exact sum is within 1e-12 of one, judged in floating point.
Prospect certainty equivalent computed on final wealth (wealth plus each prize), then the wealth taken back off.
Probability exactly zero refused as not positive, though the page allows it.
Identification check looks only at lottery A of each response, so a set whose only mixed lottery is B is refused.
Newton search stops once the largest gradient component is below 1e-2 instead of 1e-7.
The standard error of gamma applies the delta factor gamma (1 - gamma) twice.
A whole-number probability text such as "1" is refused, although the page accepts it.
The choice precision kappa is fixed at 1 and reported as 1 instead of being estimated.
The prospect certainty equivalent is returned as a final-wealth amount (starting wealth plus the change).
Prospect model refuses a lottery when wealth plus a prize is not positive, although the prospect model ignores wealth.
Likelihood uses certainty equivalents rounded to whole cents, although the likelihood must use the unrounded values.
Identification check reads only the first response, so a set whose first answer is pure is refused although a later answer is mixed.
estimate reports log kappa as kappa_hat instead of kappa, so the precision estimate can be negative.
The model-name error message omits the two allowed names, so it does not name the condition.
Each prospect value is rounded to a whole number before the inverse, a rounded intermediate that the page forbids.
CRRA wealth check tests each prize alone, not wealth plus prize, so a prize of -999 is refused at any wealth.
Gamma-zero CRRA sums the expected prize in floats, so an exact half cent can fall just below the half and round down.
The CRRA certainty equivalent is returned as final wealth, not as a change from wealth.
The Newton loop stops once the largest step is below 1e-3, before the stationary point, so the score is not zero.
The prospect value of a gain uses exponent gamma instead of 1 - gamma.
estimate never moves lambda from the starting grid value: the Newton step leaves the lambda coordinate at zero.
the maximiser takes its lambda gradient with the wrong sign, so lambda descends the likelihood.
estimate reports the log of lambda, not lambda, as lambda_hat.
Reported lambda_hat is clamped at 10 by hand, so a participant with a larger loss weight gets a wrong estimate.
Maximiser starts from the single point gamma 0.5, lambda 1, kappa 1 and never tries the grid of starts.
Prospect certainty equivalent is divided by 100 before the cent rounding, so it is returned in dollars.
Reported lambda_hat is clamped at 5 by hand, so a participant with a larger loss weight gets a wrong estimate.
The second-order search stops at the first step smaller than 1e-2 instead of 1e-10, so the point is not yet stationary.
The standard error of lambda_hat is the coordinate standard error in log lambda, not multiplied by lambda.
The standard error of kappa_hat is the coordinate standard error in log kappa, not multiplied by kappa.
The second-order search stops after three iterations and reports the point it has, converged or not.
Reported gamma_hat is rounded to two decimals before it is returned, to match a printed table.
The reported log_likelihood is evaluated with kappa fixed at 1, not at the estimated kappa.
The search takes plain gradient steps of fixed size 0.1 instead of Newton steps, and stops at the iteration limit.
The observed information is taken as the Hessian itself, without the minus sign, so the standard errors are not defined.
The standard errors are the observed information at the best grid point before the search, not at the estimate.
Standard error of gamma reported in the transformed coordinate c, without the delta-method factor gamma(1 - gamma).
Prospect certainty equivalent for a negative lottery value divides no loss weight: c = -(-V)^(1/(1-gamma)), not -(-V/lambda)^(1/(1-gamma)).
CRRA wealth check is off by one: final wealth of exactly zero cents is accepted instead of raising ValueError.
CRRA certainty equivalent returned as a float number of cents rather than an int.
Logit scale read as dollars instead of hundreds of dollars: z = kappa * dCE / 100 with dCE in cents.
estimate reports gamma_hat as the logit coordinate zeta = log(gamma/(1-gamma)), not gamma itself.
estimate clamps the reported lambda_hat at 20, while the likelihood and standard errors use the unclamped estimate.
The maximiser returns after its first Newton step from the grid start, without iterating to a stationary point.
log_likelihood skips every response whose two lotteries are both pure, so only the mixed responses enter the sum.

CRRA utility is evaluated at the prize, not at wealth plus the prize, so the wealth is left out of the utility.
A response that chose B contributes log P(A) (the logit for A) instead of log(1 - P(A)).
estimate refuses unless every response has a mixed-sign lottery, which is stricter than the page's condition.
The prospect inverse for a negative lottery value multiplies by lambda where it should divide by lambda.
The logit uses the certainty equivalents rounded to whole cents, not the unrounded values the page requires.
estimate reports the transformed coordinate zeta = log(gamma/(1-gamma)) as gamma_hat instead of gamma.
